review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the downstream files Functoriality.lean and Reconstruction.lean for uses of basicOpen. The simp-interface gaps are all around the defs `basicOpen`, `toPoint`, `ofPointIdeal` and `intersectionIdeal`, which have no membership or apply lemmas. The existing @[simp] `mem_primeFilter` is fine: it is an `Iff.rfl` rewrite to a smaller form. I did not run Lean. The suggested lemma names and forms are untested, and I did not check how they would interact with existing Mathlib simp lemmas such as `Order.Ideal.principal_le_iff`.

findings.excerpt:
def basicOpen (I : Order.Ideal A) : Set (PrimeIdealSpectrum A) :=
  {P | ¬ I ≤ P.1}
findings.problem: `basicOpen` is an exposed def with no membership lemma. Every proof that needs `P ∈ basicOpen (principal a)` unfolds the def by hand with `simp only [basicOpen, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, Order.Ideal.principal_le_iff]`. The same long simp set appears in this file at lines 221, 349, 435, 438, 444 and 446. It is copied again in Functoriality.lean (`spectrumComap_preimage_basicOpen_principal`) and Reconstruction.lean (`spaceToSpectrum_preimage_basicOpen`). Other proofs use `change`. This unfolds the definition at each use and ties the proofs to the `Set.mem_ofPred_eq` representation. The canonical normal forms are `P ∈ basicOpen I ↔ ¬ I ≤ P.1` and, for principal ideals, `P ∈ basicOpen (principal a) ↔ a ∉ P.1`. Neither is available to `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: After `basicOpen`, add `@[simp] theorem mem_basicOpen (I) (P : PrimeIdealSpectrum A) : P ∈ basicOpen I ↔ ¬ I ≤ P.1 := Iff.rfl`. Also add `@[simp] theorem mem_basicOpen_principal (a : A) (P : PrimeIdealSpectrum A) : P ∈ basicOpen (Order.Ideal.principal a) ↔ a ∉ P.1 := by rw [mem_basicOpen, Order.Ideal.principal_le_iff]`. The rewrites go to a smaller form, so there is no loop. The `simpa only [basicOpen, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, …]` calls then become `simpa using h` or `simp [mem_basicOpen_principal]`. Consider also making `basicOpen_subset_iff` a simp lemma, since its `I ≤ J` right-hand side is the normal form and it is already used by `rw` in Functoriality.lean.
findings.benefit: Proofs about the spectrum, here and in the downstream files, can use plain `simp` and no longer depend on how `basicOpen` is defined. The repeated three-lemma simp set goes away, and the preimage lemmas in Functoriality and Reconstruction get shorter.

findings.declaration: toPoint, ofPointIdeal, intersectionIdeal (missing apply/membership simp lemmas)
findings.excerpt:
def toPoint (P : PrimeIdealSpectrum A) : Locale.PT (Order.Ideal A) where
  toFun I := ¬ I ≤ P.1
findings.problem: `toPoint P I`, `a ∈ (ofPoint f).1` and `a ∈ intersectionIdeal Z` have no simp or apply lemmas. The proofs reach the underlying statements only through `change`, for example `change ¬ (¬ Order.Ideal.principal a ≤ P.1) ↔ a ∈ P.1` (line 147). Other examples: `change (¬ I ≤ ofPointIdeal f) ↔ f I` in `toPoint_ofPoint`, `change ¬ f (Order.Ideal.principal (a ⊓ b)) at hab`, `change ¬ ∀ P ∈ Z, a ∈ P.1 at ha` (line 429) and `change ¬ ∀ Q ∈ Z, a ∈ Q.1 at haP` (line 467). `simp` cannot see through these definitions. Each proof therefore has to restate the unfolded form, and a change to the representation would break all of them.
findings.proposed_change: Add the rewrite lemmas as `@[simp]`: `toPoint_apply : toPoint P I = ¬ I ≤ P.1` (or the `Prop`-level iff), `mem_ofPoint : a ∈ (ofPoint f).1 ↔ ¬ f (Order.Ideal.principal a)`, and `mem_intersectionIdeal : a ∈ intersectionIdeal Z ↔ ∀ P ∈ Z, a ∈ P.1`. All three are `Iff.rfl` or `rfl` proofs, and each rewrites a definition to its unfolded body. Then replace the `change` calls with `simp` or `rw`, e.g. `simp [mem_ofPoint, Order.Ideal.principal_le_iff]` for `ofPoint_toPoint`.
findings.benefit: Users can compute with `toPoint` and `ofPoint` through `simp` and don't need `change`. The core equivalence proofs become robust and shorter. The membership forms are also the canonical ones for the `push Not` steps in `intersectionIdeal_isPrime`.
